title: Memory leak in event listener cleanup
body:
## Bug Description

The `EventManager` class doesn't properly clean up event listeners, causing memory leaks when components are destroyed.

## Error Message

```
Test failed: Memory usage grew from 50MB to 250MB after 1000 iterations
```

## Stack Trace

```
Error: Memory leak detected
    at Object.<anonymous> (tests/eventManager.test.js:67:11)
    at runTest (node_modules/jest/runner.js:234:7)
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create 1000 EventManager instances
2. Register event listeners on each
3. Call `destroy()` on each instance
4. Observe memory usage continues to grow
5. Event listeners are not removed from internal map

## Expected Behavior

When `destroy()` is called:
1. All event listeners should be removed
2. Internal references should be cleared
3. Memory should be released for garbage collection

## Actual Behavior

The `destroy()` method clears the listeners array but doesn't remove the actual event listeners from the DOM elements or event emitters. The internal `_listenerMap` is also not cleared.

## Additional Context

- Issue is in `src/events/EventManager.js`
- The `addEventListener` wrapper stores references but `destroy()` doesn't call `removeEventListener`
- Need to track original listener references to properly clean up

## Code Location

```javascript
// src/events/EventManager.js:45
destroy() {
  this.listeners = [];  // This is not enough!
  // Missing: actual removeEventListener calls
  // Missing: _listenerMap.clear()
}
```

expected_fix.description: Properly remove event listeners and clear internal maps in destroy method
expected_fix.validation: Memory leak test should pass: memory usage should remain stable

setup_instructions: Create tests/eventManager.test.js with memory leak test
May need to run with --expose-gc flag for memory testing
